title: The last stanza
hook: sadaa sachidaanand: ever truth, consciousness and bliss, breaker of enemies, dwelling in all (Jaap 199)

segments.voice: Yesterday, chhand, and your line, march in praise. Did a walk fall into a beat? Today, after all its stanzas, Jaap comes home. Day three hundred fifty-six.

Some music ends by coming home. The orchestra has wandered through storms and dances and quiet passages, and at the end, the themes from the opening come back, gathered up, all the instruments together, one last chord. The music says: we've arrived. Jaap Sahib ends in a similar way. It doesn't introduce a stranger in its last lines. It gathers what it has said, and the languages it has said it in. Today: the last stanza.
screen: `THE THEMES COME BACK AT THE END.` → `ALL THE INSTRUMENTS TOGETHER.` → `ONE LAST CHORD.`

segments.voice: Near the very end, back in the gliding bhujang prayat where the salutations began, comes this line: sadaa sachidaanand, satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda, samastul nivaasee. Take it slowly. Sadaa: always, ever. Sachidaanand is three Sanskrit words fused: sat, truth or being; chit, consciousness; aanand, bliss. Ever truth, consciousness and bliss. Then satr pranaasee: the destroyer of enemies, the protector you met in the armed One and the breaker of the cruel. Then the language changes in mid-line. Kareemul kuninda: Kareem is Arabic, the Generous; kuninda is Persian, the Maker. The generous Maker. And samastul nivaasee: the One who dwells in all, present in every land. Listen to what just happened. In one line, Sanskrit and Arabic and Persian sit side by side, the same mix the whole hymn has used. Bliss, protection, generosity, presence everywhere: themes from all the past three weeks, gathered in one breath. That's the final chord. And the stanza that seals the hymn ends with these words: sadaa ang sange, ever with you, by your side, close as your own limbs. After stanza upon stanza of names too vast to picture, timeless, formless, king of kings, sun of suns, Jaap's last word is not far away at all. It's right here. Ever true, ever bliss, and ever beside you.
screen: `SADAA SACHIDAANAND: EVER TRUTH, BLISS.` · `KAREEMUL KUNINDA: THE GENEROUS MAKER.` · `THREE LANGUAGES IN ONE LINE.` · `SADAA ANG SANGE: EVER BY YOUR SIDE.` · then, large: `EVER TRUE, EVER BLISS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say the last line aloud. Slowly, in the snake's rhythm: sadaa sachidaanand, satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda, samastul nivaasee. Say it twice. Then say the sealing words once, gently: sadaa ang sange. Ever by your side. Put a hand on your arm or over your heart as you say it, and feel how close that is. Then sit with the closeness. The bell holds the time.
Sadaa. Always, ever — it opens Jaap's final chord: ever truth, consciousness and bliss, the generous Maker dwelling in all, and ever by your side.
Your line: ever true, ever bliss. Today, at one ordinary moment, a red light, a queue, a kettle, remember: sadaa ang sange, ever beside you. Day three hundred fifty-six.

screen: `DAY 356 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: JAAP AND THE AMRIT BOWL.`

howItsDone: Sikhs end their morning recitation of Jaap Sahib with these closing stanzas, often reciting them from memory, before moving on to the Tav Prasad Savaiye.

match.prompt: the last stanza — tap the pairs.

myth: Jaap ends by introducing a brand-new idea
it gathers its themes and its languages into one final chord.
the closing line mixes Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian words
sachidaanand, kareem and kuninda sit side by side.
Jaap's last word puts the One far away
sadaa ang sange: ever beside you, close as your own limbs.

fork.setup: after stanza upon stanza of vast names, timeless, formless, king of kings, how does Jaap end?
options: with the One even farther away.
with the One ever beside you: sadaa ang sange.
with silence and no final line.
fork.reveal: the vast One of every name turns out, in the last line, to be close as your own limbs.

original.note: Gurmukhi: sadaa, always, ever; it opens sadaa sachidaanand and sadaa ang sange.

trapdoor: what you thought: the last stanza is just where the hymn stops.
what it means: it gathers Jaap's themes and languages into one chord, and ends with the One ever by your side.
what a scholar hears: 'sadaa sachidaanand … kareemul kuninda samastul nivaasee' fuses the Vedantic sat-chit-ananda with Arabic karim and Persian kunindah in a single bhujang prayat line.

sources.ref: Jaap Sahib, closing stanzas (198–199): sadaa sachidaanand satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda samastul nivaasee; sadaa ang sange

notes: Numbering: the outline places 'sadaa sachidaanand' at Jaap 199. In common editions the 'sadaa sachidaanand … samastul nivaasee' line may be stanza 198, with 199 beginning 'chatar chakkar vartee' and ending 'sadaa ang sange abhangang bibhoote'. The voice says 'near the very end' and 'the stanza that seals the hymn' to avoid a wrong number. Confirm.
Glosses: satr pranaasee (destroyer of enemies), kareemul kuninda (generous Maker, Arabic karim + Persian kunindah), samastul nivaasee (dwelling in all): confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer tells the listener what they feel or claims all long hymns end this way; 'every language' overclaim now 'three languages'; dropped stanza counts (199, ninety-some) from the voice and fork; cut 'a line many Sikhs treasure'.
